Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:10:1.hebrew: תנינא - פלוגתא אחריתי במתני' בתנאי אחריני, ולמה ליה לרבי למיתני לתרתי בבי? ניתני התם לגבי ר' יהושע: וכן היה ר' יהודה אומר כדבריו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:10:1.english: We already learned [this] - [Even though it is] a different dispute in the Mishnah with other Tannaim, why did Rebbi need to teach two clauses? Let him teach there regarding Rabbi Yehoshua: “And so Rabbi Yehuda would say in accordance with his statement.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:10:2.hebrew: שהוא בלא יבא - אע"פ שאינו אלא בלאו, הולד ממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:10:2.english: Who is [born of a union prohibited] by “he shall not enter” - Even though it is only a negative commandment, the offspring is a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:11:1.english: Any [union] for which they are liable - For that act of intercourse, [they are liable to] karet at the hand of Heaven.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:11:2.hebrew: כל שחייבין עליו מיתת ב"ד - אבל חייבי כריתות — לא, וטעמא דכולהו מפרש ביבמות (שם):
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:11:2.english: Any [union] for which one is liable to court-imposed capital punishment - But [those born of unions] liable to karet are not [mamzerim]; and the reason for all of them is explained in Yevamot (ibid).

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:12:1.hebrew: זה בזה - הם בממזרים, וממזרים בהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:12:1.english: One another - They [may marry] with mamzerim, and mamzerim with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:13:1.hebrew: אי הכי אמאי ר' יהודה אוסר - הני ודאי לא איקרי קהל, דהא לא חזו לבא בקהל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:13:1.english: If so, why does Rabbi Yehuda prohibit - These certainly are not called a “congregation,” for they are not fit to enter into the congregation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:13:2.hebrew: ה"ק - כלומר, וכולה חד תנא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:13:2.english: This is what he is saying - That is to say, the entire [mishna] is [the view of] a single tanna.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:14:1.hebrew: בן ט' שנים ויום אחד - שהוא גר עמוני וכו', דבכי האי זימנא חזי לביאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:14:1.english: A boy nine years and one day [old] - [Meaning] that he is an Ammonite convert, etc., for at this age he is fit for intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:14:2.hebrew: פסלוה - לכהנת מן התרומה ומן הכהונה, ולויה וישראלית מלינשא עוד לכהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:14:2.english: They disqualified her - For a priest's daughter, from [eating] terumah and from the priesthood; and [for] a Levite woman and an Israelite woman, from ever marrying a priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:14:3.hebrew: כל שזרעו פסול - מן הכהונה, פוסל את אשתו מן הכהונה. ולקמן מפרש מאי בינייהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:14:3.english: Whoever's offspring is disqualified - [That is, disqualified] from the priesthood, [he] disqualifies his wife from the priesthood. And later [the Gemara] explains what is [the difference] between them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:1:1.hebrew: ודלא כר"ש - דאמר לקמן בפירקין (קידושין דף עח.): גיורת פחותה מבת ג' כשירה לכהונה. וה"ק: כל האסורין לבא בקהל כהונה — ומאי ניהו דמרבי האי כללא יתר על הראשונים שאסורין בקהל ישראל? גיורת שפחותה מבת שלש שנים, וכ"ש יתירה על בת שלש שנים — מותרין הנך אסורין, גיורות וממזרים ונתיני ושתוקי, לבא זה בזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:1:1.english: And not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - For he says later in our chapter (Kiddushin 78a): A female convert [who converted at] less than three [years of age] is fit for the priesthood. And this is what [the mishna] is saying: “All those who are forbidden to enter the congregation of the priesthood” — and what is it that this generalization includes beyond the former [groups] who are forbidden [to enter] the congregation of Israel? A female convert who is less than three years [old], and all the more so [one who is] older than three years — these forbidden [individuals] — female converts, mamzerim, Netinim, and shetukim — are permitted to marry one another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:2:1.hebrew: ונוקמה בבת שלש - ולא בפחות, ונימא דפחותה מותרת לכהן, ובה לא איירי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:2:1.english: And let us establish it with [a girl of] three [years] - And not with [one] younger [than this], and let us say that [a girl] younger [than this] is permitted to a priest, and [the Mishnah] is not dealing with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:2:2.hebrew: א"כ - דכר"ש מיתוקמא, דפחותה מותרת לכהונה, והוא לא התיר לבא בממזרת אלא האסורין לבא בכהונה — הוי משמע: האי דפחותה אית ליה דאסורה לממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:2:2.english: If so - That [if] it is established in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, where [a female convert who is] less [than three years old] is permitted to [marry into] the priesthood, and he did not permit marrying a mamzeret except to those who are forbidden to marry into the priesthood — it would imply that [regarding] this [case of a girl who is] less [than three years old], he holds that she is forbidden to [marry] a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:2:3.english: From its side it is broken - Its refutation is ready at its side.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:4:1.hebrew: אסורין לבא זה בזה - בתמיה: היא בממזר, וממזר בה? "והרי גיורת וכו'" — דכיון דקהל גרים לאו קהל הוא, לא שנא פחותה, ל"ש יתירה. ועל כרחיך תנא דידן, מדשרי יתירה על בת שלש לממזר, ש"מ אית ליה קהל גרים לא איקרי קהל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:4:1.english: Are prohibited to marry one another - [This is asked] in astonishment: [Is] she [prohibited] to a mamzer, and a mamzer to her?! “And behold, a [female] convert, etc.” — for since the congregation of converts is not [considered] a “congregation,” there is no difference [whether she is] younger [than three years old], nor is there a difference [whether she is] older. And perforce, our Tanna, since he permitted [a female convert] older than three years [old] to a mamzer, learn from this that he holds [that] the congregation of converts is not called a “congregation.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:4:2.hebrew: והרי גר כו' - כיון דאית ליה: קהל גרים לא איקרי קהל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:4:2.english: And behold, a convert, etc. - Since [the Tanna] holds [that] the congregation of converts is not called a "congregation".

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:5:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב נתן - לא תימא כל האסורין, דתקשי לך אלמנה לכ"ג, ותיקשי לך גר מדוקיא; אלא ה"ק ת"ק: כל שבתו אסורה לכהונה — ומאי ניהו דמוסיף האי כללא על האסורין לישראל? גר שנשא גיורת, וכר' אליעזר בן יעקב, דאמר במתני' (לקמן קידושין דף עז.): גר שנשא גיורת בתו פסולה לכהונה — מותרים לבא זה בזה. והיינו: גר מותר בממזרת, וממזר בו. דאילו בגר שנשא ישראלית, לא מצית לאוקמה, דמאן שמעת ליה דאמר כהן אסור לישא בתו? ר' יהודה, דאמר במתני' (שם): בת גר זכר כבת חלל זכר; ומדסיפא ר' יהודה, דקתני: ר' יהודה אוסר — רישא לאו ר' יהודה; להכי מוקמי לה כר"א בן יעקב. ושמעיה ר' יהודה לת"ק דאית ליה קהל גרים לא איקרי קהל, ופליג עליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:5:1.english: Rather, Rav Natan said - Do not say [that the phrase] 'all who are forbidden' [means those forbidden to the priesthood], for [the case of] a widow to a High Priest would pose a difficulty to you; and [nor say that it means those forbidden to enter the congregation, for] a convert [would pose] a difficulty to you from the inference [that he would be forbidden to marry a female mamzer]. Rather, this is what the First Tanna is saying: Anyone whose daughter is forbidden to the priesthood — and who is that, whom this generalization adds beyond those forbidden to [an ordinary] Israelite? A convert who married a female convert, and in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov, who said in the Mishnah (below, 77a): 'A convert who married a female convert, his daughter is disqualified from the priesthood' — are permitted to marry one another. And that is: a convert is permitted to [marry] a female mamzer, and a mamzer to him [i.e., to marry a female convert]. For as for a [male] convert who married an Israelite woman, you could not establish it [as referring to him], since whom did you hear who says that a priest is forbidden to marry his daughter? Rabbi Yehuda, who said in the Mishnah (there): 'The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male chalal'; and since the latter clause is Rabbi Yehuda, as it teaches: 'Rabbi Yehuda prohibits,' the first clause is not Rabbi Yehuda; therefore, we establish it in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov. And Rabbi Yehuda heard the First Tanna, who maintains that the congregation of converts is not called a 'congregation,' and he disputed with him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:6:1.hebrew: וכללא הוא - בתמיה: דכל האסורין לכהן מותרין לממזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:6:1.english: And is it a principle - [This is asked] in astonishment: That all those forbidden to a priest are permitted to [marry] a mamzer?

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:6:2.hebrew: כר' דוסתאי בר' יהודה - ס"ל לתנא דידן, דאמר (שם): בנות ישראל מקוה טהרה לחללים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:6:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Dostai ben Rabbi Yehuda - Our Tanna holds [in accordance with him], who said (there [below, 77a]): The daughters of Israel are an immersion pool of purification for ḥalalim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:7:1.hebrew: ותו הא המותר - לישא כהן בתו, אסור לבא באסורין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:7:1.english: And furthermore: Is [one who is] permitted - [Meaning, is one whose] daughter a priest is permitted to marry, prohibited from marrying into [those of] forbidden [lineage]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:7:2.hebrew: והרי גר שנשא בת ישראל כו' - ומותר לבא בממזרים, דהא אמר: קהל גרים לאו קהל הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:7:2.english: And behold, a convert who married an Israelite woman, etc. - And he is permitted to enter [into marriage] with mamzerim, for behold, it said: "The congregation of converts is not a congregation."

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:8:1.english: A mamzer from a married woman - [This is an example of a union punishable by court-imposed] death [penalties].

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:8:2.english: A mamzer from his sister - [Punishable by] excision.

Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:8:3.hebrew: איכא בינייהו - לאו בגר איפליגו, אלא דקסבר: יש ממזר מחייבי כריתות. וה"ק: כל הנולדים מאיסורי ערוה ממזרים הם, ומותרים לבא זה בזה — הני חייבי כריתות בבני חייבי מיתות, כגון א"א — דכולן ממזרים הם. ור' יהודה אוסר לבא חייבי כריתות בבני חייבי מיתות, דקסבר: אין ממזר אלא מחייבי מיתות. וטעמא מפורש ביבמות (דף מט.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 74b:8:3.english: [The difference] between them - They did not disagree regarding a convert; rather, [the first tanna] holds that there is a mamzer [produced] from [unions liable to] excision. And this is what he is saying: All those born from forbidden sexual relations are mamzerim, and they are permitted to marry one another — these [offspring of unions liable to] excision with the offspring of [unions liable to] court-imposed death, such as [that of] a married woman — as they are all mamzerim. And Rabbi Yehuda forbids those [offspring of unions liable to] excision to marry into the offspring of [unions liable to] court-imposed death, as he holds that a mamzer is only [produced] from [unions liable to] court-imposed death. And the reason is explained in Yevamot (49a).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:11:1.hebrew: מאי קא משמע לן תנינא כו' ר' יהושע אומר כל שחייבין עליו מיתת בית דין - ופירושו: כמו "תנינא חדא זימנא" דלעיל דאבא שאול, דהוה ליה למיתנייא התם גבי מילתא דר' יהושע: "וכן היה ר' יהודה אומר כדבריו". וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך למיפרך "תנינא"? ליפרך דר' יהודה אדר' יהודה! דהכא קאמר ר' יהודה דאין ממזר אלא מחייבי מיתות ב"ד, ובמסכת יבמות (דף מט.) קאמר: "לא יגלה כנף אביו" איירי באנוסת אביו שהיא בלאו, וסמיך ליה "לא יבא ממזר" — משמע שממזר הוה אפי' מחייבי לאוין, דהא ר' יהודה נמי דריש סמוכים במשנה תורה! וי"ל: דר' יהודה סבר התם, דאשת אב דכתיב בין "לא יקח" ובין "לא יגלה" הוי מיותר; דהשתא, אנוסת אביו לא יקח, כדכתיב "לא יגלה כנף אביו" — אשתו מיבעיא?! וא"כ, למידרשיה ולומר ד"לא יבא ממזר" דוקא מאשת אביו, ולימא הכי: מ"לא יקח" עד "לא יגלה", דהיינו אשת אביו — הוי ממזר; טפי לא הוי ממזר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:11:1.english: "What is [this] teaching us? We already learned: etc., Rabbi Yehoshua says: Any [offspring of a union] for which one is liable to court-imposed capital punishment" - And its explanation is like "we already learned this once before" above regarding Abba Shaul, for it should have been taught there, alongside the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua: "And so Rabbi Yehuda would say in accordance with his words." And if you say: Why was it necessary to object with "we already learned"? Let it rather object from [a contradiction between one statement of] Rabbi Yehuda and [another statement of] Rabbi Yehuda! For here Rabbi Yehuda says that there is no mamzer except from those liable to court-imposed capital punishment, whereas in Tractate Yevamot (49a) it says: "He shall not uncover his father's cloak" speaks of a woman raped by his father, who is [prohibited only] by a negative commandment, and juxtaposed to it is: "A mamzer shall not enter," which implies that a mamzer results even from those liable for [violating] negative commandments, for Rabbi Yehuda also expounds juxtapositions in Mishneh Torah! And one can say: Rabbi Yehuda holds there that [the mention of] his father's wife, which is written between "he shall not take" and "and he shall not uncover," is superfluous; for now [that] he may not take a woman raped by his father, as it is written: "he shall not uncover his father's cloak" — is [his father's married] wife needed [to be stated]?! And if so, [it is available] to be expounded and to say that "a mamzer shall not enter" [applies] specifically to his father's wife, and let it say thus: From "he shall not take" until "he shall not uncover" — which is his father's wife — [the offspring] is a mamzer; beyond that, [the offspring] is not a mamzer.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:1:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר כל האסורים לבא בקהל כהונה ומאי נינהו גיורת פחותה כו' - וא"ת: אמאי לא פריך, "הא תנא ליה רישא דגר מותר בממזרת", כדפריך לעיל? וי"ל: דלאו עיקר קושיא היא דפריך "הא תנא ליה רישא", אלא עיקריה — אאידך קושיא סמיך: "ר' יהודה אוסר, אהייא":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:1:1.english: "This is what it is saying: All those who are prohibited to enter into the congregation of the priesthood; and who are they? A female convert less than [three years and one day old, etc.]" - And if you say: Why did [the Gemara] not object, "Didn't [the Mishnah] already teach in the first clause that a convert is permitted to [marry] a mamzeret?", just as it objected above? And one can say: That which it objected, "Didn't it teach [this in] the first clause?", was not the primary difficulty; rather, its primary [difficulty] relied upon the other question: "'Rabbi Yehuda prohibits' — to which [case does this refer]?"

Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:4:1.hebrew: והרי גר דמותר בכהנת ומותר בממזרת - וא"ת: מאי פריך? והרי הטעם שהוא מותר, לפי שלא הוזהרו כשרות להינשא לפסולים, ולא משום הכשר גר הוא, דלעולם אמרינן דכהן אסור בגיורת! ו"מותר אסור", ר"ל: כל שמותר לבא בקהל מטעם יחוס, אסור ליקח ממזרת! ונראה לפרש: הרי גר שנשא בת ישראל, שהבת מותרת לכהן ומותרת בממזר, כר"א בן יעקב; וכה"ג פריך בסמוך:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:4:1.english: "And behold, a convert, who is permitted to [marry] a daughter of a priest and is permitted to [marry] a mamzeret" - And if you say: What is [the Gemara's] objection? For behold, the reason that he is permitted [to marry her] is because [women of] fit [lineage] were not cautioned against marrying disqualified [men], and it is not on account of the fitness of the convert [himself], for we always maintain that a priest is forbidden [to marry] a female convert! And [the inference that] "one who is permitted is forbidden" means: anyone who is permitted to enter the congregation [of the priesthood] by virtue of [fit] lineage is forbidden to take a mamzeret! And it seems [correct] to explain: [The Gemara's objection refers to the case of] a convert who married an Israelite woman, where the daughter is permitted to a priest and is permitted to a mamzer, in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov; and [the Gemara] objects in a similar manner nearby.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:7:1.hebrew: דת"ק סבר ממזר מאחותו הוי ממזר - ואם תאמר: היכי משתמע פלוגתייהו ממתני'? ופירש הקונטרס דה"ק: כל הנולדים מאיסור ערוה ממזרים הם ומותרים לבא זה בזה, בני חייבי כריתות בבני חייבי מיתות, עכ"ל. ולא נהירא, דדוחק הוא. לכך פר"י דה"ק: כל האסורין לבא בקהל שאפילו קידושין אין תופסין בהם, כגון חייבי כריתות, מותרין לבא זה בזה; כלומר, כל שבא מאיסור תפיסת הקידושין — דהיינו בני חייבי כריתות וחייבי מיתות דאין קידושין תופסין בהם — כולן מותרין לבא זה בזה, דקסבר יש ממזר מכל דבר דלא תפסי קידושין. "מאי קא משמע לן תנינא כו' ר' יהושע אומר כל שחייבין עליו מיתת בית דין" — ופירושו כמו "תנינא חדא זימנא" דלעיל דאבא שאול, דהוה ליה למיתנייא התם גבי מילתא דר' יהושע: וכן היה ר' יהודה אומר כדבריו. וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך למיפרך "תנינא"? ליפרך דר' יהודה אדר' יהודה! דהכא קאמר ר' יהודה דאין ממזר אלא מחייבי מיתות ב"ד, ובמסכת יבמות (דף מט.) קאמר "לא יגלה כנף אביו" איירי באנוסת אביו שהיא בלאו, וסמיך ליה "לא יבא ממזר", משמע שממזר הוה אפי' מחייבי לאוין, דהא ר' יהודה נמי דריש סמוכים במשנה תורה! וי"ל: דר' יהודה סבר התם דאשת אב דכתיב בין "לא יקח" ובין "לא יגלה" הוי מיותר, דהשתא אנוסת אביו לא יקח כדכתיב "לא יגלה כנף אביו", אשתו מיבעיא?! וא"כ, למידרשיה ולומר ד"לא יבא ממזר" דוקא מאשת אביו; ולימא הכי: מ"לא יקח" עד "לא יגלה" — דהיינו אשת אביו — הוי ממזר, טפי לא הוי ממזר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:7:1.english: That the first tanna holds [that] a mamzer from his sister is a mamzer - And if you say: How is their dispute inferred from the Mishnah? And Rashi explained that this is what it is saying: All those born of a prohibited incestuous union [ervah] are mamzerim, and they are permitted to marry one another — the offspring of those liable to karet [may marry] the offspring of those liable to [court-imposed capital] punishment, until here is his wording. And this is not plausible, as it is forced. Therefore the Ri explained that this is what it is saying: "All those who are prohibited to enter into the congregation" — [meaning unions where] even betrothal [kiddushin] does not take effect with them, such as those liable to karet — "are permitted to enter with one another"; that is to say, anyone who comes from a prohibition of the taking effect of betrothal — that is, the offspring of those liable to karet and those liable to capital punishment, with whom betrothal does not take effect — they are all permitted to marry one another, for he holds that there is a mamzer from anything where betrothal does not take effect. "[Regarding the Gemara's question:] What does this teach us? We [already] learned: [...] Rabbi Yehoshua says: Anyone [born of a union] for which they are liable to court-imposed capital punishment" — and its meaning is like "We [already] learned it once" mentioned above regarding Abba Shaul: that it should have taught there, next to Rabbi Yehoshua's statement: "And so Rabbi Yehuda used to say in accordance with his words." And if you say: Why was it necessary to object "We [already] learned [this]"? Let it object from Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda! For here Rabbi Yehuda says that there is no mamzer except from those liable to capital punishment of the court, whereas in tractate Yevamot (49a) he says [that the verse]: "nor reveal his father's garment" deals with a woman raped by his father, which is [prohibited merely by] a negative commandment, and adjacent to it is "A mamzer shall not enter," which implies that a mamzer is [produced] even from those liable to negative commandments, since Rabbi Yehuda also expounds juxtapositions in Deuteronomy! And one can say: Rabbi Yehuda holds there that [the mention of] a father's wife written between "shall not take" and "nor reveal" is superfluous; for now, [if] he may not take a woman raped by his father, as it is written: "nor reveal his father's garment," is his [father's] wife necessary [to state]? And if so, [the phrase is available] to expound it and to say that "A mamzer shall not enter" [applies] specifically to [the offspring of] his father's wife; and let it say thus: From "shall not take" until "nor reveal" — that is, his father's wife — he is a mamzer; beyond that, he is not a mamzer.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:9:1.hebrew: דת"ק סבר ממזר מאחותו הוי ממזר - ואם תאמר: היכי משתמע פלוגתייהו ממתני'? ופירש הקונטרס, דה"ק: "כל הנולדים מאיסור ערוה ממזרים הם ומותרים לבא זה בזה, בני חייבי כריתות בבני חייבי מיתות", עכ"ל. ולא נהירא, דדוחק הוא. לכך פר"י, דה"ק: כל האסורין לבא בקהל שאפילו קידושין אין תופסין בהם, כגון חייבי כריתות — מותרין לבא זה בזה; כלומר: כל שבא מאיסור תפיסת הקידושין — דהיינו בני חייבי כריתות וחייבי מיתות דאין קידושין תופסין בהם — כולן מותרין לבא זה בזה, דקסבר: יש ממזר מכל דבר דלא תפסי קידושין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 74b:9:1.english: That the first tanna holds [that] a mamzer from his sister is a mamzer - And if you say: How is their dispute inferred from the Mishnah? And Rashi explained that this is what it is saying: "All those born of an incestuous prohibition [ervah] are mamzerim and are permitted to marry one another — the offspring of those liable to karet with the offspring of those liable to court-imposed death penalties"; thus far his words. But this is not plausible, for it is forced. Therefore, the Ri explained that this is what it is saying: All those who are forbidden to enter the congregation [in such a manner] that even betrothal does not take effect with them, such as those liable to karet, are permitted to marry one another. That is to say: Anyone who was born from a prohibition where betrothal does not take effect — that is, the offspring of those liable to karet and those liable to court-imposed death penalties, with whom betrothal does not take effect — they are all permitted to marry one another, for he holds: a mamzer is produced from any [forbidden union] where betrothal does not take effect.
